sources.title: Batch 0060 frozen MySQL isolation repository context
MySQL 8.4 InnoDB isolation primary-source research packet

claims.text: The candidate names all four InnoDB isolation levels in increasing isolation order and identifies REPEATABLE READ as the default while noting that global/session/next-transaction settings can override the default for a concrete connection.

The answer distinguishes READ COMMITTED from REPEATABLE READ through InnoDB consistent-read snapshot lifetime: RC gets a fresh snapshot per consistent read while RR reuses the first consistent-read snapshot in the transaction.

The candidate keeps ordinary consistent nonlocking SELECT behavior separate from locking reads and DML, and explains that RR range locking can use record/gap/next-key locks rather than attributing every phantom-related behavior solely to MVCC or solely to next-key locking.

The answer describes SERIALIZABLE as stricter than RR and notes the plain-SELECT to SELECT FOR SHARE behavior with autocommit disabled, framing higher isolation as a consistency/concurrency tradeoff rather than an unconditional upgrade.
